source.title: Inference Optimal VLMs Need Fewer Visual Tokens and More Parameters
source.authors: Kevin Y. Li; Sachin Goyal; João Dias Semedo; J. Kolter

page_placements.theme: Inference-optimal allocation depends on task and cost accounting

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law analysis to visual-language models and inference-time compute, using downstream error rather than language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study fits inference-time downstream-error scaling laws over LLM parameter count and visual-token count, checks a prediction at 14B, and reports OCR and compression-method variants. It does not test held-out pretraining cross-entropy or training-compute allocation. The token-compression algorithm comparisons and ablations are not cataloged as scaling-law results. The reported finding that alternative fitting solvers produced varying solutions is noted in method_sensitivity but not given a separate row because numerical fit outcomes are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study fits power-law scaling of downstream error in VLMs against LLM parameter count and visual-token count. It then checks the fit's prediction at 14B. That bears on V6, downstream predictability with scale, in a new setting. Its exponents shift with task family, compression method and fitting choice, which bears on V7. It does not measure pretraining loss or training-compute allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that for visual reasoning the inference-optimal VLM uses the largest feasible LLM with very few visual tokens (often one). OCR tasks instead need many tokens. Their fitted law predicts 14B performance within 2%, and token compression research should target extreme compression ratios.
record.recipe_differences: Fits downstream error as a function of LLM parameter count and visual-token count for VLM inference; uses visual-reasoning/OCR benchmarks and a grid-search fit rather than held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponents differ between visual reasoning and OCR tasks, and between TokenPacker and PruMerge fits. The compute-optimal visual-token count changes with text-query length (Q=0 versus Q=50). The authors state that SciPy curve fitting and gradient-based solvers were unstable and produced varying solutions; they use grid search instead.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed inference FLOPs, visual-reasoning error is minimised by the largest LLM with about 1 visual token (Q=0), or about 16 tokens (Q=50). For OCR tasks the optimum is the opposite.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-compute-optimal VLMs trade visual tokens for LLM parameters, with the optimum depending on text-query length and task family.

record.problems: The scaling-law fits use a grid search with coarse stated parameter ranges; statistical uncertainty or error bars for fitted exponents are not reported. The main metric is an aggregate downstream-error measure on selected benchmarks, not held-out pretraining loss. The 14B extrapolation is reported as less than 2% error, without a stated uncertainty interval.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-law results left out. Token-compression method comparisons and component ablations in Sections 4 and Appendix A.4 are excluded because they evaluate compression methods rather than the scaling behavior or prediction claims cataloged here.

untested.parts: Pretraining cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of loss across orders of magnitude; only a 2x downstream extrapolation is tested.
Training-compute-optimal allocation of parameters versus tokens.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Pretraining-loss power laws in other modalities or regimes. The VLM fits are downstream error at inference.
Predictability from pretraining loss; text-only LLM downstream tasks.
Disagreement between published training laws; effects of parameter counting, schedule and data choice; curvature of training-loss curves.

missing.what: Fit-solver instability: SciPy curve fitting and gradient-based solvers gave varying solutions, so grid search was used, with coarse ranges α,β∈[0,0.1]. No numeric fits from the alternative solvers are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The laws here are inference-time downstream-error laws for VLMs, not pretraining-loss laws, so links to V6 and V7 are by analogy of form. The 14B check is only a 2x extrapolation. No uncertainty is given for the exponents.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or training compute.
Extrapolating pretraining loss from small language-model runs to much larger runs.
Training-compute-optimal allocation between language-model parameters and pretraining tokens.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes, including image/video pretraining, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer.
Predictability from pretraining loss, and downstream-task predictability for text-only language models or other downstream settings.

Whether published language-model training laws disagree, effects of parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, and data choices, and whether training-loss curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 VLMs (aggregate fit over 0.5B, 1.8B, 4B, and 7B backbones)
rows.operation_detail: Fit the proposed downstream-error scaling law against LLM parameters and visual-token count using TokenPacker compression.

conditions.value: average normalized error over nine visual-reasoning benchmarks

rows.measure: Fitted scaling parameters for average downstream error
rows.note: One aggregate fit across the listed model sizes and benchmarks. The authors state α is more than five times β, indicating downstream error changes faster with LLM parameters than with visual tokens in this setting.
rows.check: This is the reference fit. For V7 it serves only as the comparison baseline for r3, r4 and r5. It fits the inference-time downstream-error law, not a pretraining-loss law.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 14B VLM
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate a scaling-law prediction fitted on VLMs with 0.5B–7B backbones against the 14B model at varying visual-token counts.
rows.measure: Error between predicted and actual downstream performance
rows.note: The reported prediction is for downstream performance, not pretraining loss.
rows.check: The extrapolation is from 7B to 14B, about 2x and not orders of magnitude, so it does not bear on V2. The error is 'less than 2%' with no uncertainty stated.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 VLMs (aggregate fit on DocVQA and TextVQA)
rows.operation_detail: Fit the proposed downstream-error scaling law on OCR-style benchmarks.
rows.measure: Fitted scaling parameters for average downstream error
rows.note: The authors state there are no significant average downstream-performance gains from increasing LLM parameters on these OCR tasks; visual-token count predominantly dictates performance. This is a task-dependent contrast with the visual-reasoning fit.
rows.check: For V6, the authors report no significant gains from LLM size on OCR tasks. α = 0.029 is small, but visual-token scaling still dominates. For V7, the same row shows exponents shifting with task family, which is consistent with V7.

source_check.correct: For V6's LLM-size effect: absent, as the authors report no significant gains. For V7: observed, because the fitted exponents change from visual reasoning (α=0.077, β=0.015) to OCR (α=0.029, β=0.048).
source_check.problem: The shared absent state fits the LLM-size result for V6 but misrepresents the observed setup dependence for V7.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 VLMs with LLaVA-PruMerge (aggregate fit)
rows.operation_detail: Fit scaling-law exponents for PruMerge while reusing the A, B, and D constants from the TokenPacker fit.

conditions.value: A, B, D reused from Section 3.3

rows.note: Authors describe α as comparable and β as lower than in the TokenPacker fit.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 VLMs with LLaVA-PruMerge (aggregate fit)
rows.operation_detail: Refit the scaling law from scratch for PruMerge.
rows.measure: Fitted scaling parameters for downstream error
rows.note: The authors say the error varies around two times faster with LLM parameters than with tokens in this refit, versus more than five times faster in their TokenPacker visual-reasoning fit.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 VLMs (aggregate inference-optimal trade-off)
rows.operation_detail: Determine the downstream-error-minimizing allocation between LLM parameters and visual tokens at fixed inference compute.
rows.value: Use one visual token with the largest LLM that fits the inference budget.
rows.note: This concerns inference-time VLM allocation, not training-compute-optimal allocation between parameters and pretraining tokens.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5 VLMs (aggregate inference-optimal trade-off)
rows.operation_detail: Determine the downstream-error-minimizing allocation between LLM parameters and visual tokens at fixed inference compute.
rows.value: The optimal visual-token count is around 16.
rows.note: The text says optimal visual-token count rises with text-query length; this is an inference-time VLM trade-off, not the training-compute allocation in V3.
